fields.label: Apportionment method
fields.value: Montana uses a single sales factor (receipts factor) apportionment formula to apportion business income. Property and payroll factors are excluded.
fields.source_citation: 2025 Montana Form CIT Corporate Income Tax Instructions
fields.quote: Senate Bill 124 from the 2023 Montana Legislative session changed the apportionment of income from the three-factor, double-weighed sales method to the single-sales factor method.

fields.label: Forms
fields.value: Corporations calculate apportionment on Schedule K of Form CIT, attaching Schedule K-Combined if more than one unitary group member has Montana activity. Pass-through entities compute apportionment on Schedule K of Form PTE.
fields.source_citation: 2025 Montana Form CIT Corporate Income Tax Instructions
fields.quote: For combined filers with more than one company with Montana activity, enter the total of line 18 from Schedule K-Combined on page 11 of Form CIT.

fields.label: Income/franchise tax nexus
fields.value: Any C corporation actively engaging in business in Montana is subject to corporate income tax, and generally any activity beyond the solicitation of sales of tangible goods creates nexus. Montana has no factor-presence or bright-line economic nexus dollar or transaction thresholds.
fields.quote: In-State Activities That Create Nexus Generally, any activity performed in Montana other than the solicitation of sales of tangible goods creates nexus and a filing requirement.

fields.label: Sales/use tax: economic nexus
fields.value: Montana does not impose a general sales or use tax. Consequently, there are no remote seller economic nexus sales thresholds, transaction counts, or measurement periods.
fields.source_citation: Sales Tax Guidance for Montana Business and Residents

fields.label: P.L. 86-272
fields.value: Montana respects P.L. 86-272 immunity for out-of-state entities limited to the solicitation of orders for sales of tangible personal property sent out of state for approval and fulfillment. Montana establishes specific lists of protected, unprotected, and de minimis activities, and applies the Finnigan rule for unitary groups.
fields.quote: Public Law 86-272 provides an additional protection from state income tax.

fields.label: Individual income tax
fields.value: For 2025, Montana taxes ordinary income at 4.7% and 5.9%, with the top bracket starting at $21,100 for single filers and $42,200 for married couples filing jointly. Net long-term capital gains are taxed at preferential rates of 3.0% and 4.1%.
fields.quote: Ordinary Income Tax Rate First $21,100 of Montana Ordinary Income 4.7% Montana Ordinary Income exceeding $21,100 5.9% 2025 Net Long-Term Capital Gains Tax Rates — Single and Married Filing Separately.

fields.label: Corporate income/franchise tax
fields.value: Montana imposes a corporate income tax of 6.75% of taxable income, or 7% for corporations making a water's edge election, subject to a $50 minimum tax. Corporations meeting specific small gross sales criteria may elect an alternative 0.5% gross sales tax rate.

fields.label: Individual due date and extension
fields.value: Individual income tax returns for calendar-year filers are due April 15, with an automatic six-month filing extension to October 15. The extension applies only to filing, and any tax owed must still be paid by April 15.

fields.label: Pass-through entity tax (PTET)
fields.value: Montana provides an elective pass-through entity tax at a rate of 5.9% of each electing owner's distributive share of Montana-source income. The irrevocable election is made annually by an eligible partnership or S corporation directly on a timely-filed Form PTE.
fields.source_citation: Montana Pass-Through Entity Tax: How to Elect & Pay
fields.quote: The pass-through entity tax (PTET) is a 5.9% of an affected owner’s distributive share of Montana source income.

fields.label: Key forms
fields.value: Key individual income tax forms include Form 2, Form IT, and Form EST-I. Primary business forms include Form CIT for corporations and Form PTE for pass-through entities.
